abstract:
We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity.
  In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.
